body:
### Description

Hi devs

I was using `cupy.matmul` and got out-of-memory errors when using generic ubuntu.

The same code strangely works on ubuntu WSL2, with a GPU that has the same amount of memory.

Also, although on WSL2 that both `matmul` calls would work, the 2nd way (`ab_bad = cp.matmul(a_bad, b_bad)`) is a lot slower than the 1st way (`ab_ok = cp.matmul(a_ok, b_ok)`).
I guess the time different might makes sense for they were possibly executed differently, but on the other hand the two ways are essentially doing the same thing here...

thank you for looking into this!

the error message i got
```
Traceback (most recent call last):

cupy.cuda.memory.OutOfMemoryError: Out of memory allocating 5,440,000,000 bytes (allocated so far: 2,315,200,512 bytes).
```


### To Reproduce
(please play with `s0, s1, s2, s3` if your setup has a lot of memory, my configs are quite limited to 4GB of VRAM)
```py
import cupy as cp

s0, s1, s2, s3 = 500, 80, 3400, 5
dtype = cp.complex64

# ok
a_ok = cp.ones((s0, s1, s2), dtype=dtype)
b_ok = cp.ones((s0, s2, s3), dtype=dtype)

ab_ok = cp.matmul(a_ok, b_ok)

print(f'{a_ok.shape, b_ok.shape, ab_ok.shape}')

# fail
a_bad = cp.ones((s0, 1, s3, s2), dtype=dtype)
b_bad = cp.ones((s0, s1, s2, 1), dtype=dtype)

ab_bad = cp.matmul(a_bad, b_bad)

print(f'{a_bad.shape, b_bad.shape, ab_bad.shape}')
```


### Installation

Wheel (`pip install cupy-***`)
